blocks.h2: Installing a Heater in a Condo Closet
blocks.body: A closet installation has a few requirements: room for the heater and service access, proper venting or an electric model, a drain pan with a drain line where possible and a way to get the old tank out and the new one in. In a walk-up building, that might mean three flights of stairs. We plan the size, the route and the timing before install day, so the swap goes smoothly.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a New Water Heater
blocks.body: Size, fuel and venting come first. Closet installs may need a drain pan and a compact model. Stairs and building rules can affect labor. We check everything and quote one flat price.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Installation Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: Will a new heater fit in my condo closet?
items.answer: We measure the closet and the path in before we quote, and we'll recommend a model that fits.

items.q: Do I need a drain pan?
items.answer: If the heater sits above another unit or finished space, a pan with a drain is strongly recommended.

items.q: Can you install a bigger heater after our renovation?
items.preview: Usually, if the space and venting allow.
items.answer: Usually. We check the space, venting and gas or electric supply first.

items.q: Do you remove the old heater?
items.answer: Yes, including carrying it out of the building.

items.q: Can I switch from gas to electric?
items.answer: Sometimes, if the electrical service can support it. We'll check.

items.q: How much does water heater installation cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on size, type and venting. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the size, fuel type, venting and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
